subtitle: The Poet of Vallabhi Who Hid Grammar Inside War and Exile

panels.shot: dramatic three-quarter view of Bhatti seated before a palm-leaf manuscript, dim lamplight, shadowed pillars of Vallabhi’s hall rising behind him
panels.action: Bhatti sits cross-legged in a stone hall of Vallabhi, stylus poised over palm leaves, as faint visions of Rama, Sita and Ravana loom like translucent silhouettes behind him.

dialogue.text: In Vallabhi’s quiet halls, c. 600 CE, Bhatti does something daring: he turns the Ramayana itself into a living textbook of grammar, poetics and language.

i18n.hi: शांत वल्लभी में, लगभग ६०० ई., भट्टी साहस करता है – वह रामायण को ही बना देता है जीवित किताब: व्याकरण, काव्य और भाषा की।

panels.shot: slow push-in from wide cityscape to interior, documentary-style
panels.action: A sweeping view of Vallabhi’s coastal city—monasteries, royal halls, scribes at work—then into a calmer inner chamber where Bhatti studies palm-leaf bundles.

dialogue.text: Under the Maitrakas of Vallabhi, scholars debate dharma, kingship and language. In this world of learning, Bhatti asks a simple question: how should grammar be taught?

i18n.hi: वल्लभी के मैत्रक राज में विद्वान धर्म, राजसत्ता और भाषा पर बहस करते हैं। इसी विद्या-सभा में भट्टी पूछता है: व्याकरण कैसे पढ़ाया जाए?

panels.shot: medium shot over Bhatti’s shoulder, manuscript foregrounded
panels.action: Over Bhatti’s shoulder we see neat columns of Sanskrit on a palm leaf, beside a copy of a grammatical sutra text in tighter script.

dialogue.text: Panini’s sutras rule the language of the age. They are precise, compressed, powerful—yet hard to hold in the mind of a young student.

i18n.hi: पाणिनी के सूत्र युग की भाषा चलाते हैं। नापतौल में सही, गुँथे, ताक़तवर – पर नव-शिष्य के दिमाग़ में टिकना मुश्किल।

panels.shot: close-up on Bhatti’s contemplative face, light and shadow
panels.action: Bhatti gazes at the manuscripts, brows slightly furrowed, as dust from a sunbeam cuts across his face in the quiet room.

dialogue.speaker: bhatti
dialogue.text: Rules alone fade. A story stays.

i18n.hi: सिर्फ़ नियम धुंधले पड़ जाते हैं। कहानी टिक जाती है।

panels.shot: low-angle wide shot, Bhatti rising to his feet
panels.action: Bhatti rises, holding a palm leaf bearing verses of the Ramayana, behind him a mural-like relief of Rama stringing his bow.

dialogue.text: The Ramayana is already sung in courts and hermitages. Bhatti sees an opening: bind dry rules to living heroes, and let memory ride on emotion.

i18n.hi: रामायण राजदरबारों और आश्रमों में गाई जा रही है। भट्टी राह देखता है: सूखे नियमों को जीते-जागते नायकों से बाँधो, याद को भावनाओं पर सवार कर दो।

panels.shot: wide shot of Vallabhi audience hall, subtle bird’s-eye tilt
panels.action: In a Maitraka hall lined with columns, Bhatti stands before a small circle of students and fellow poets, palm leaf in hand, as they listen intently.

dialogue.text: He chooses a form the age respects: the mahakavya, the grand courtly epic. But his aim is unusual—to make every canto carry a lesson in language.

i18n.hi: वह युग के मान्य रूप को चुनता है: महाकाव्य, राजदरबारी महागाथा। पर उसका लक्ष्य अलग है – हर सर्ग को भाषा का पाठ बना देना।

panels.shot: medium shot, Bhatti seated and writing, side profile
panels.action: Bhatti sits again, now composing with steady focus, his hand moving across fresh palm leaves as a small oil lamp burns beside him.

dialogue.text: He begins the Bhattikavya, also called the Ravanavadha, retelling Rama’s tale so that grammar and poetics quietly shape every turn of the story.

i18n.hi: वह शुरू करता है ‘भट्टिकाव्य’, जिसे ‘रावणवध’ भी कहते हैं — रामकथा को यूँ सुनाते हुए कि व्याकरण और काव्यशास्त्र हर मोड़ को चुपचाप सँवारें।

panels.shot: close-up on manuscript where a verse is being inscribed
panels.action: An extreme close-up of Bhatti’s stylus as it etches a line about Rama into the leaf, with faint marginal symbols indicating grammatical points.

dialogue.text: In one section, he chooses tenses and voices to match action; in another, he threads figures of speech through battle. The poem performs the rules it teaches.

i18n.hi: कहीं वह क्रियाकाल और वाच्य को क्रिया से मिलाता है; कहीं अलंकारों की धार को युद्ध में पिरोता है। कविता खुद वही नियम निभाती है जो वह सिखाती है।

panels.shot: slow push-out from leaf to room of learners
panels.action: The image pulls back from the leaf to show young learners around Bhatti, reciting verses with fingers counting off grammatical forms.

dialogue.text: Students repeat Rama’s exile and Ravana’s fall. As they chant, they also rehearse Paninian forms and poetic devices, almost without noticing.

i18n.hi: विद्यार्थी राम का वनवास और रावण का अंत दोहराते हैं। गाते-गाते वे पाणिनीय रूपों और काव्य-युक्तियों का अभ्यास भी कर लेते हैं, लगभग बेख़बर।

panels.shot: high-angle shot of Vallabhi royal presence, Bhatti in front
panels.action: A regal figure sits on a slightly raised seat in Vallabhi’s audience hall, while Bhatti stands below, respectfully offering the bound leaves of his work.

dialogue.text: The poem’s own verses later name Vallabhi and a patron—read as Narendra by some, linked to Dharasena by others. The record keeps the exact name uncertain.

i18n.hi: काव्य की ही पंक्तियाँ बाद में वल्लभी और एक संरक्षक का नाम देती हैं—किसी के अनुसार ‘नरेन्द्र’, किसी के अनुसार ‘धारसेन’। लिखित प्रमाण नाम को धुंधला ही रखता है।

panels.shot: medium shot, Bhatti reading aloud, with courtly listeners
panels.action: Bhatti recites from his manuscript before courtiers and monks, their faces reflecting both aesthetic delight and scholarly curiosity.

dialogue.text: What is clear is the setting: a learned court at Vallabhi, c. 600–650 CE, where poetry, philosophy and grammar meet in the same hall.

i18n.hi: जो साफ़ है, वह मंच है: वल्लभी का विद्वान दरबार, लगभग ६००–६५० ई., जहाँ कविता, दर्शन और व्याकरण एक ही सभा में मिलते हैं।

panels.shot: symbolic split-screen-style composition within one frame
panels.action: On one side of the frame, Rama’s army marches stylized across a painted panel; on the other side, Bhatti’s hand annotates grammatical points beside those verses.

dialogue.text: Bhatti’s choices are deliberate. He aligns narrative episodes with particular rules, so each canto becomes a kind of lesson wrapped in emotion and rhythm.

i18n.hi: भट्टी की हर चाल सोची-समझी है। वह कथा-प्रसंगों को ख़ास नियमों से जोड़ता है, ताकि हर सर्ग भाव और लय में लिपटा एक पाठ बन जाए।

panels.shot: medium-wide of a later generation teacher using the text, Bhatti’s image faded in background
panels.action: A later Sanskrit teacher in simple robes guides pupils through a copy of the Bhattikavya while a faint, almost ghostly mural of Bhatti presides behind them.

dialogue.text: Over the centuries, scribes copy his epic and commentators explain how each section illustrates grammar. The work becomes a classic example of teaching inside story.

i18n.hi: सदियों तक लिपिक उसके महाकाव्य की नकल करते हैं और भाष्यकार बताते हैं कि हर अंश कौन सा नियम दिखा रहा है। यह रचना कहानी के भीतर पढ़ाने की मिसाल बन जाती है।

panels.shot: close-up on a later commentator’s manuscript margin
panels.action: A palm leaf from a later era shows Bhatti’s verses in the center, with compact marginal notes pointing out rules and poetic ornaments.

dialogue.text: Other theorists of the age—like Dandin in his Kavyadarsha—discuss what makes great poetry. Bhatti’s poem stands among such works as a lived example.

i18n.hi: इसी युग के अन्य विचारक—जैसे दण्डी ‘काव्यादर्श’ में—महान कविता की कसौटी बताते हैं। भट्टी का काव्य ऐसी ही रचनाओं के बीच जीती-जागती मिसाल बनकर खड़ा है।

panels.shot: wide shot transitioning from ancient scriptorium to modern archive
panels.action: A visual dissolve from an ancient scriptorium where palm leaves are stacked, to a modern-style shelf of bound volumes, with Bhattikavya placed among them.

dialogue.text: Modern editors and translators still return to this Vallabhi epic, reading it both as Ramayana retelling and as a crafted guide to Sanskrit usage.

i18n.hi: आज भी संपादक और अनुवादक इस वल्लभी-महाकाव्य पर लौटते हैं—इसे एक ओर रामकथा-प्रस्तुति, दूसरी ओर संस्कृत-प्रयोग की तराशा हुई मार्गदर्शिका मानकर पढ़ते हैं।

panels.shot: final contemplative close-up of Bhatti’s face looking slightly away, timeless background
panels.action: Bhatti’s face is shown in serene close-up, half-lit, as behind him the faint outlines of script, bows, and ocean waves merge into a single abstract backdrop.

dialogue.text: Bhatti’s life beyond his verses stays mostly hidden, but his choice is clear: he trusted that knowledge endures when bound to story, and that memory deepens when grammar moves with feeling.

i18n.hi: पंक्तियों के बाहर भट्टी का जीवन ज़्यादातर ओझल रहा, पर उसकी पसंद साफ़ है: उसने भरोसा किया कि ज्ञान टिकता है जब कहानी से बँधता है, और स्मृति गहरी होती है जब व्याकरण भाव के साथ चलती है।

title_i18n.en: Bhatti Turns Grammar into an Epic
title_i18n.hi: भट्टी ने व्याकरण को बना दिया महाकाव्य

subtitle_i18n.en: The Poet of Vallabhi Who Hid Grammar Inside War and Exile
subtitle_i18n.hi: वल्लभी का कवि जिसने युद्ध और वनवास में छुपा दी व्याकरण
